subject: CALL statement
notes:
PB55 FOLD (2026-10-15, owner decision 2026-08-08 'THE RULE IS THE UNIT'): the transcription printed this rule's nested list(s) at column 0, so 3 sub-item(s) held rows of their own; indented at their measured printed level, they are this rule's body and their adjudications are folded here, nothing dropped.

[the rule's own record before the fold]
The two residuals this row carried are closed. (a) 3c: the implementor-defined runtime-resource set of a CALL is the stack the activation needs (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-14, kb/Work PB2659): ProgramTable.CallProgram asks ActivationStack.IsAvailable first and raises EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES (golden 2002/pb2659_call_resources_recursion, ON EXCEPTION at the exhausted depth). The GR3i boundary mark is an exception filter, so a condition crossing many boundaries is not rethrown once per boundary. (b) 3d's DESCRIPTION half on the dynamic Format-1 lane: now checked at activation under the enabled-in-both gate (14.8.2.3.2 / 14.8.2.3.3 rule 1 length, 14.8.2.2 group rule; golden 2002/pb165_dynamic_call_description_check, kb/Work PB165 w1015w). The Format-2 lane whose callee has no compile-time signature (a program-specifier resolved against an external repository, 12.3.8.4 GR10 c)) is the prototype registry's residual, recorded on SR-14.9.4.3-25 (b), not on this row's legs.

[folded GR-14.9.4.4-L2.1 = §14.9.4.4 3) h) 1.: CONFORMS]
GR3h item 1 has TWO conditions and the emitted CALL now expresses both, plus GR3i's precondition that they only apply to a program that was NOT successfully called. (i) FAMILY: 'if the exception condition is any of the EC-PROGRAM or EC-EXTERNAL exception conditions' - the arm that flags the phrase is now `catch (CobolCallException __cp) when (!__cp.ControlTransferred && CobolCallException.IsProgramOrExternal(__cp.EcName))`, and EnabledProgramNames() asks the SAME predicate, so the compile-time split and the runtime filter cannot drift (CallExceptionCarrierDriftTests.IsProgramOrExternal_PartitionsTheCarriedNames). Previously the arm was `catch (CobolCallException)` with no filter at all, so EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND (8.4.3.2.4 GR6b) ran imperative-statement-1; measured live and now fixed - CallOnException_IsNotEnteredByFunctionNotFound. (ii) PHRASE: 'and an ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified' - the arm is emitted on `c.OnException is not null`, never on the NOT phrase (see L2.3). (iii) SCOPE: item 1 governs only a failed ACTIVATION. The try block spans the callee's whole execution, so the arm also needs to know whether control had been transferred; ProgramTable.CallProgram now marks CobolCallException.ControlTransferred on anything escaping inst.Call, and 14.9.4.4 GR3e's external-conformance check moved OUT of the callee body onto ICobolProgram.DescribeExternals(), which the boundary calls BEFORE Call - GR3e precedes GR3g's transfer, so an EC-EXTERNAL raise stays attributable to this CALL (ec_external_format_conflict still green). Item 1 carries no checking-enabled qualifier, so the phrase arm is emitted with NO status Set; the enabled subset is caught one arm earlier, where 14.6.13.1.1 does require the Set. kb/Work PB233.

[folded GR-14.9.4.4-L2.2 = §14.9.4.4 3) h) 2.: CONFORMS]
Item 2 is a DISJUNCTION under 'If checking for the exception condition is enabled', and BOTH halves are now implemented by the same emitted arm shape, chosen at compile time from the statement's enabled set. HALF (A) - an EC-PROGRAM/EC-EXTERNAL condition with no ON EXCEPTION phrase - was already verified and is unchanged in substance, but its trigger was wrong: EmitProgramEcCatch took `hasPhrase` (ON *or* NOT ON), so a NOT-ON-only CALL took the phrase arm and never reached the declaratives. It now takes `byPhrase: c.OnException is not null`, which is what the rule and 14.6.13.1.3 #1 both say; CallNotOnExceptionOnly_Enabled_RunsTheDeclarativeAndSkipsTheNotPhrase and the golden's section A pin it, including 'control is then transferred to the end of the CALL statement' - the NOT phrase does not run, because every catching arm sets the failure flag the NOT block is guarded on. HALF (B) - 'or if the exception condition is not one of the EC-PROGRAM exception conditions' - had NO implementation and now has one: EnabledOtherCallNames() selects the statement's enabled names that a CobolCallException can carry but that are not in the two families (today EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND), and emits a SECOND arm whose body is always the 14.9.49 Format-3 selection with the fatal default - never the phrase, exactly as the rule requires. That needed a binder half too: EcBinder.QueryFor(BoundCallProgram) queried only ProgramNames+ExternalNames, so >>TURN EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND CHECKING ON produced no BoundEcChecked wrapper at all; a user-FUNCTION activation (IsFunction) now also queries FunctionActivationNames (8.4.3.2.4 GR6b -> GR6f, 'any declarative ... associated with that exception condition is executed'). FunctionNotFound_Enabled_RunsTheDeclarative and the golden's section D pin it. The dispatch-result protocol is unchanged: >=0 RESUME AT, -2 RESUME NEXT falls to the end of the CALL, anything else re-throws the fatal default (14.6.13.1.3 #5/#7). kb/Work PB233.

[folded GR-14.9.4.4-L2.3 = §14.9.4.4 3) h) 3.: CONFORMS]
Item 3 ('If checking for the exception condition is not enabled, subsequent behavior is as specified in 14.6.13.1') and the whole of GR3i. Item 3's disposition for a fatal condition is 14.6.13.1.3 #8, implementor-defined; this implementation defines it as the loud abnormal termination ProgramTable.RunMain applies to an unhandled CobolCallException. The defect was that a CALL written with ONLY `NOT ON EXCEPTION` never reached item 3: `hasPhrase` was true, an unfiltered catch swallowed the failure, no `if (__callErr)` block existed to run, and the run unit continued as if the CALL had succeeded - measured live (BEFORE/AFTER, exit 0, against exit 1 for the identical phrase-free CALL). 14.6.13.1.3 #1 settles it independently of GR3h: only 'a conditional phrase WITHOUT the NOT phrase' processes a fatal condition. The catch is now emitted on `c.OnException is not null`; with neither an ON phrase nor an enabled name, the CALL emits the bare invocation and the NOT body unguarded, which is the phrase-free path exactly. GR3i's other half - 'If the program was successfully called ... the ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored' - was also unimplemented: the try spans the callee's execution, so ANY unhandled CobolCallException from inside a callee ran the ACTIVATOR's imperative-statement-1 and the run unit survived. The activation boundary now marks ControlTransferred (see L2.1) and every arm filters on `!ControlTransferred`, so such a condition falls through to 14.6.13.1. GR3i's NOT-ON half (imperative-statement-2 on a non-exception return) and the propagated-condition half (EmitPropagationPickup) are unchanged and still pinned by ec_external_format_conflict and the golden's section C. kb/Work PB233.
